title: Pure-loss bosonic dynamic capacities: EPnI consequences and consumed-key secrecy accounting
author: Alec Kriebel
page_title: Pure-loss bosonic dynamic capacities and consumed-key secrecy | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: An EPnI-based consequence for pure-loss bosonic capacity trade-offs, with average photon constraints and explicit consumed-key secrecy accounting.
abstract: The finite-energy multimode entropy photon-number inequality proved in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies the sharp entropy premise in the previously conditional pure-loss bosonic dynamic-capacity converses. We give its precise classical, quantum and entanglement consequence under an average photon constraint, including arbitrary entanglement across uses. For public, private and secret-key resources, an operational correction is necessary: the printed catalytic secrecy condition of Wilde–Hsieh protects consumed key jointly with generated secrets and excludes the one-time pad. A zero-energy converse disproves the displayed region under that literal condition. We establish the formula with an explicit generated-secret secrecy criterion, corrected converse accounting, and direct key-assisted coding. The formulas and original conditional reductions are inherited; this is a consequence and operational audit, not an independent proof of EPnI. We rely on the cited unrefereed EPnI proof. Its analytical arguments and formal-source semantics were audited, but its Lean build was not reproduced.
accessible_explanation: A lossy optical channel can carry classical information, quantum information and shared resources in different combinations. This note spells out the consequences of a cited finite-energy multimode entropy theorem for those trade-offs under an average photon budget. It also examines how a security definition changes when a protocol consumes a secret key.
central_result: Using the cited unrefereed OpenAI finite-energy multimode EPnI theorem, the note derives the established classical/quantum/entanglement capacity region for a pure-loss channel with transmissivity between one half and one. For public/private/secret-key rates, it distinguishes the literal secrecy condition that protects consumed resources jointly from a changed convention protecting only generated secrets. The paper gives a zero-energy obstruction to the former and states the capacity formula under the latter, with a rewritten converse and direct key-assisted coding.
conditionality: The exact capacity conclusions depend on the soundness and stated scope of the external multimode EPnI theorem and the named coding results. The note provides no independent proof of EPnI. Its elementary consumed-key obstruction does not depend on EPnI.
limitations: One-mode pure-loss channel with independent vacuum environment; 1/2 ≤ η ≤ 1 and finite average photons N per use.
The photon budget is averaged over messages, key and encoder randomness; arbitrary entanglement across channel uses is permitted.
Signed forward net resource accounting uses finite gross rates and charged finite seeds; no free feedback or superlinear catalysts.
The positive private theorem uses generated-secret uniform-message trace secrecy; it does not preserve the secrecy of consumed key after use or establish semantic security.
No stronger energy constraint, two-way-assisted, thermal-channel quantum-capacity, amplifier or confidential-broadcast result is asserted.
The paper reports that the upstream Lean build was not reproduced. No formal machine verification of the capacity consequences is claimed.
